corrected_text: Steel tempered to the degree fit for watch springs acquires a strong magnetism, which it exhibits immediately on the removal of the magnet. But it diffuses very fast; and, in a very few minutes, it is reduced to less than one half of its intensity while in contact with the magnet, and not two thirds of what it was immediately on removal from it. It continues to diffuse for some days, though the bar be kept with care; but the diffusion diminishes fast, and it retains at least one third of its greatest power for any length of time, unless carelessly kept or injudiciously treated.
